title: Oral Literature in Africa
abstract: Ruth Finnegan’s Oral Literature in Africa was first published in 1970, and since then has been widely praised as one of the most important books in its field. Based on years of fieldwork, the study traces the history of storytelling across the continent of Africa. This revised edition makes Finnegan’s ground-breaking research available to the next generation of scholars. It includes a new introduction, additional images and an updated bibliography, as well as its original chapters on poetry, prose, ‘drum language’ and drama, and an overview of the social, linguistic and historical background of oral literature in Africa.

narrative:
Short impact summary

Oral Literature in Africa (2012), published by Open Book Publishers, has been cited 720 times — enough that OpenAlex puts it in the top 1% of works in its field and year. Beyond that, it has been downloaded 128,844 times.

Full narrative

Oral Literature in Africa by Ruth Finnegan was published by Open Book Publishers in 2012. It is part of the World oral literature series series. Conceptually, the work connects to Sierra leone, Drama, Poetry, History and Drum.

OpenAlex records 720 citations. That places it in the top 1% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2015 with 42 citing works. Notable citing venues include Unisa Institutional Repository (University of South Africa), Research in African Literatures and Journal of African Cultural Studies. The citing works include 545 journal articles, 103 dissertations, 40 book chapters and 19 books. They come from 40 countries, led by South Africa, the United States and Nigeria.

It has been downloaded 128,844 times via Google Books and OAPEN. Open Library reports a combined count of 8 reading logs and catalog editions. Its subject matter aligns with Quality Education among the Sustainable Development Goals.
